name: Glider
description:
Kid-safe slot-together glider: a fuselage with a round nose and a fin, a wing and a tail that slide through slits in the fuselage. It flies a bit better than a paper airplane because its center of gravity and wing angles are built in.
Print flat without supports in PLA, 0.2 mm layers, 100 % infill (the balance assumes solid parts): about 4.7 m of filament. Press a 2 cent euro coin flat into the round pocket in the nose; it is the nose weight, and the total mass with the coin is about 17 g. The mini plate (70 %, about 2.3 m of filament) is a cheap test print: it takes a 1 cent euro coin, and its total mass with the coin is about 9 g. Fix the coin with a drop of glue or a piece of tape before giving the glider to small children: a loose coin is a choking hazard. Slide the tail through the rear slit and the wing through the front slit until both are centered (notch marks on the wing and the tail).
Launch: pinch the body below the wing, about a third back from the wing's leading edge (near the balance point), with the wings level and the nose 5-10° down, and give it a gentle push at jogging speed. If it dives, bend the tail's trailing edge up slightly; if it climbs and stalls, bend it down. Don't throw at people, and throw away broken parts: broken PLA can be sharp.
